solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bottle with boiling soup — great work!

parts.note: a magnum is a large wine bottle holding two standard bottles

indicators.note: boiling suggests the letters of soup are bubbling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cook who has served soup and a big bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling' turns SOUP into OPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names an artist's or writer's masterpiece, the finest of their output.

clue.text: Lab rat harassed around English province

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the abbreviation for English
harassed suggests the letters of lab rat are hounded into a new order

explanation.surface: A laboratory rat is pestered around an English place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harassed' rearranges LAB RAT; 'around' places E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of Canada's prairie provinces, with Edmonton as its capital.

clue.text: New organ with shiny top is arriving soon

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: top means the first letter of shiny, its head in a down entry

explanation.surface: A brand-new church organ with polished pipes is about to be delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach or draw close to a point in time or place is the verb sense.

clue.text: A little bit more, half imaginatively styled

indicators.note: half means the first two of the four letters of more are kept
imaginatively says the letters of styled are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for a bit more, styled half with imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imaginatively' rearranges STYLED into DESTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to a limited or moderate degree means only slightly.

clue.text: 25 winner somehow entrapping Potus

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the two following words are arranged in some new way

explanation.surface: A contest winner is somehow trapping the President of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is EUROVISION; Sandie Shaw won it for the UK in 1967 with this song. POTUS is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: The song took the 1967 Eurovision title for the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Being responsible for 5 in hospital finishes May

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
dies means comes to an end or finishes
may is the hawthorn blossom, and haw is the hawthorn's berry or the tree itself

explanation.surface: Someone responsible for a patient in hospital finishes in May.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is PUPPET ON A STRING, the UK's 1967 Eurovision winner; the capital in May hides the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The British singer performed that song barefoot and won the contest with it.

clue.text: Sometimes before that is appropriate

definitions.meaning: the word that comes before 'That' in the name of the British boy band ... That
as a verb, to appropriate is to seize or help oneself to

explanation.surface: A grammar note about when it is fitting to use a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Take That is a British boy band of the 1990s onward; 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing something for oneself is to help oneself to it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Test says to replace current crossing

indicators.note: to replace says one word swaps in for a letter within the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is the physics symbol for electric current
avers means states or says

explanation.surface: An exam paper says a current must be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps I in TRIAL for AVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey across something is a noun sense, as in a traverse of a glacier.

clue.text: Soul Train destroyed by devastating hurricane

parts.note: in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double or soul

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of train are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: The TV music show Soul Train being wrecked by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Soul Train was a US dance music TV show; 'Soul' is split off, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2005 storm devastated New Orleans and the US Gulf Coast.

clue.text: A big brown alligator heads for group of 13

indicators.note: heads means the front letter of each of the four words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a large brown alligator, oddly linked to a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is WATERLOO, the song with which the Swedish band won Eurovision in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish pop quartet won with that song, so they are the band behind it.

clue.text: 500 bits of bling broken by European children, presumably

indicators.note: broken by says the string formed so far is split open with the next piece set into the gap

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
pendants are pieces of showy jewellery hung on chains

explanation.surface: Five hundred pieces of jewellery are smashed by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' puts E between D and PENDANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Children usually rely on their parents for support, hence the hedging 'presumably'.

clue.text: Violently grabs weak supports

parts.note: rests are props or supports, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: A description of someone grabbing at flimsy props in a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something away forcibly with a twisting motion is the sense here.

clue.text: Huge story about fish starting measles outbreak

indicators.note: about says the long story is wrapped around the remaining pieces

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic tale
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of measles is used

explanation.surface: A big news story about fish leading to a measles outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' seems to belong to the measles scene, but it is the definition; 'about' wraps the story round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread sudden spread of disease is exactly what the medical term names.

clue.text: Had gutless rival in court battle

indicators.note: in says the eating and the gutted rival sit inside the word for courting

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
had, as in had dinner, means ate

indicators.note: gutless means the inner letters of rival are removed, leaving its outside pair

explanation.surface: Someone describes a feeble opponent in a legal or sporting contest at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the eating and the gutted rival inside the courting word. It is also the 1974 Eurovision winner, linking to 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat in 1815 took place near the Belgian town of that name.

clue.text: Dons motley actor used

indicators.note: motley means mixed and varied, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jester puts on the patchwork costume an actor has worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like a verb meaning puts on, but is the noun for university teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: University lecturers, especially at Oxford and Cambridge, are called dons.

clue.text: See 6
Finishing room at home in bluish-green

indicators.note: in says the room and home pieces sit inside the colour word

parts.note: teal is a dark bluish-green colour
in means at home

explanation.surface: A decorator is finishing a room in a home, painted blue-green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the room and home pieces inside the colour; 'Finishing' looks like the decorator's work but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something final, at the end, is the adjective sense, as in a terminal stage.

clue.text: Oddly loud double 25 winner

indicators.note: double says the pair of kept letters is written out twice
oddly means the first and third letters of loud are kept

explanation.surface: A noisy duplicate is being described, in clipped terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish singer shared the 1969 Eurovision title in a four-way tie with Boom Bang-a-Bang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish pop singer was one of four joint winners of the song contest in 1969.

clue.text: Not the same as having some immune quality

indicators.note: having some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something differs because it has a degree of immunity.
explanation.definitionFit: Different in amount or size is the plain synonym sense.

clue.text: Flea's suggestion one might turn over

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says a fresh arrangement of the four letters l, e, a, f, and that arrangement gives flea

explanation.surface: A flea making a proposal that someone might reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue word FLEA is its result.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn over a fresh page is the idiom for reforming one's behaviour and starting again.

clue.text: Come to mutually satisfactory solution with American politician receiving nothing

indicators.note: receiving says the politician takes in the round letter for nothing

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A US politician gets nothing out of a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' places O inside GREEN, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling on terms both sides accept is the phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: Nasty sort of killer hides up around Mile End

indicators.note: around says the turned word wraps the final letter of mile
up says the hiding places are read upwards, from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: lairs are hiding places of animals

indicators.note: End means the last letter of Mile

explanation.surface: A vicious killer hides around Mile End, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAIRS into SRIAL; 'around' places E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer who kills repeatedly over time is called this kind of killer.

clue.text: Books on period being immoral

indicators.note: on means the books come after the period, as in an across entry

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Reading books over a long stretch of time is called immoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-indulgent and morally degenerate is the sense, as in a corrupt era.

clue.text: Sleepy maiden's back, not having succeeded being gracious

indicators.note: back says the whole string so far is read from right to left
not having says the letter for succeeded is taken out of the sleepy word

parts.note: drowsy means sleepy
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A sleepy girl is said to be back, unsuccessful but gracious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes S from DROWSY, leaving DROWY; 'back' turns DROWY plus M around.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'Gracious me!'

clue.text: Signals a couple of bits of velvet used to be clothes

indicators.note: clothes means the past-tense verb wraps round the velvet letters like a garment

parts.note: was means used to be

indicators.note: a couple of bits of means the first two letters of velvet are taken

explanation.surface: Velvet scraps used to be made into clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb: the past tense wraps round the first two letters of velvet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures of the hand, as in greeting or warning, are signs made by moving it.

clue.text: Song contest makes Rio envious

indicators.note: makes says the letters of the two words are rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: A singing competition stirs jealousy in Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges RIO ENVIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual European televised song competition is the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: Compete with opinion

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: An instruction to argue alongside one's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A point of judgement held by someone, as in 'in my opinion', is the sense.

clue.text: Calls with missing book lengths

indicators.note: with missing says the abbreviation for book is dropped from the calls

parts.note: bells are phone calls, as in 'give me a bell'

explanation.surface: Phone calls made without a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give someone a bell' is British slang for phoning them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth length, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Allowing latitude for one signal I disrupted

parts.note: for one means for example, e.g.

indicators.note: disrupted says the letters of signal and I are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Giving someone freedom, with a disrupted signal getting through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' turns SIGNAL I into ALISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something lawful is permitting it, a near synonym of allowing.
